articles.title: Hackers Used Meta’s AI Support Bot to Seize Instagram Accounts
articles.summary: Microsoft just patched a record-breaking 200 vulnerabilities in one Patch Tuesday, because why fix security incrementally when you can let it all pile up like dirty laundry? Three dozen earned the coveted 'critical' rating — aka the 'we're probably already pwned' tier.

articles.title: Victory! 702 has Expired!
articles.summary: CISA contractor casually yeeted AWS GovCloud keys and agency secrets onto public GitHub because apparently cybersecurity agencies can't secure their own contractors. Congress is rightfully losing their collective shit over this galaxy-brain move.

articles.title: Yes to California's Bill to Ban Surveillance Pricing
articles.summary: Section 702's warrantless surveillance authority finally expired, giving Americans a brief moment to breathe before Congress inevitably resurrects this constitutional vampire. The EFF is celebrating like it's 1776 all over again.

articles.title: Claude Fable 5 Doesn't Change the Mythos Security Story
articles.summary: ShinyHunters exploited an Oracle ERP zero-day to ransack American universities, because apparently higher education needed another reason to cry about budgets. Nothing says 'pursue knowledge' like having your entire student database stolen.

articles.title: The Right’s “Election Fraud” Cry for Midterms Previewed in Primaries
articles.summary: Senator Whitehouse demands ICE prove it hasn't been infiltrated by white supremacists after The Intercept exposed their recruitment materials being celebrated by neo-Nazis. Shocking absolutely no one who's been paying attention.

articles.title: A Point-by-Point Breakdown of Trump’s Failed Iran War Objectives
articles.summary: Hakeem Jeffries finally grew a spine and rallied Democrats against extending domestic surveillance laws, proving that even centrist politicians can occasionally remember the Constitution exists. Better late than never, we guess.

articles.title: Google Sues Chinese Smishing Network Accused of Using Gemini AI in Phishing
articles.summary: Over 400 Arch Linux AUR packages got hijacked to deploy credential stealers and eBPF rootkits, because even the elitist Linux users aren't safe from supply chain attacks. Your custom kernel won't save you from social engineering, btw.

articles.title: Agentjacking Attack Tricks AI Coding Agents Into Running Malicious Code
articles.summary: Chinese hackers backdoored Linux PAM and OpenSSH for nearly a decade, hiding in plain sight at the authentication layer like digital ninjas. This is why we can't have nice things — or secure login systems, apparently.

articles.title: Oracle warns of PeopleSoft zero-day breaches #tech
articles.summary: CISA issued a 72-hour patch-or-die ultimatum for an actively exploited Ivanti flaw, because apparently government agencies need stern parental supervision to apply security updates. Sunday deadline means some sysadmins are working weekends again.

articles.title: Google says ShinyHunters hackers targeting education sector via Oracle exploit
articles.summary: Oracle's PeopleSoft got demolished by a zero-day that ShinyHunters used to breach 100+ organizations, proving that enterprise software security is still stuck in the dial-up era. Oracle's 'unbreakable' marketing aged like milk in the sun.
